questions.q: What is the purpose of the base case in a recursive function?
options: To allocate additional activation frames on the call stack.
To return a result without making further recursive calls.
To divide the input into smaller subproblems for processing.
questions.fact: The base case is a stopping condition that returns a result without making further recursive calls.
why: Allocating stack frames happens during recursive calls, not at base cases.
The base case halts recursion by returning a concrete value immediately.
Dividing input into subproblems is the responsibility of the recursive case.

questions.q: What happens to the call stack when a recursive call completes and returns?
options: Its frame remains on the stack for future function calls.
All stack frames across the entire program are erased simultaneously.
Its activation frame pops off the stack and resumes caller.
questions.fact: Returning from a recursive call pops its frame off the call stack and resumes the caller.
why: Returned frames are destroyed to free memory rather than retained.
Only the returning frame is removed; caller frames remain intact.
Popping the frame frees local variables and transfers control to caller.

questions.q: What are the time and auxiliary space complexities of calculating factorial recursively?
options: O(n) time and O(n) stack space.
O(n log n) time and O(1) stack space.
O(2ⁿ) time and O(n) stack space.
questions.fact: Calculating factorial recursively has a recurrence of T(n) = T(n - 1) + O(1), running in O(n) time and O(n) stack space.
why: Factorial makes n linear recursive calls, each adding one stack frame.
Linear recursion does not split inputs to achieve O(n log n) time.
Factorial does not branch into multiple calls, so time is not O(2ⁿ).

questions.q: When is a recursive call considered tail recursive?
options: When the call occurs within an iterative loop structure.
When the recursive call is the very last operation performed before returning.
When two recursive calls branch simultaneously in the function body.
questions.fact: Tail recursion occurs when the recursive call is the very last operation performed before returning.
why: Tail recursion is a property of function calls, not while loops.
A call is tail recursive if no work remains after it returns.
Branching calls are tree recursion, not tail recursion.

questions.q: How can some compilers optimize a tail-recursive function?
options: By executing multiple recursive branches in parallel threads.
By memoizing every subproblem result in a hash map.
By reusing the stack frame in O(1) auxiliary space.
questions.fact: Some compilers can optimize tail-recursive calls to run in O(1) auxiliary stack space like a loop.
why: Tail-call optimization does not parallelize execution across threads.
Memoization caches results; tail recursion reuses existing stack frames.
Reusing the caller's frame avoids stack growth, behaving like an iterative loop.

questions.q: Can every recursive algorithm also be implemented iteratively?
options: Yes, using an explicit stack or loop construct.
No, tree traversals can only run via recursion.
Only if the function performs exactly one recursive call.
questions.fact: Every recursive algorithm can also be implemented iteratively using an explicit stack or loop.
why: Any recursion can be simulated iteratively with loops and explicit stacks.
Tree traversals can be implemented iteratively using explicit stack data structures.
Multi-branching recursion can also be converted using explicit stack tracking.

questions.q: What role does the recursive case perform in a recursive function?
options: It checks whether stack memory has enough capacity left.
It breaks input into smaller subproblems and calls itself.
It immediately returns the final accumulated computation result.
questions.fact: The recursive case breaks the input into smaller subproblems and calls the function again.
why: Operating systems manage stack capacity; functions do not poll memory size.
The recursive case reduces the problem toward the base case condition.
Returning the final result without calls is the base case role.
